calls.reconciliation: All three runs used the same AAII sent_results data and converged on median -9 with a 10-90 width of 30-31. Factual differences were trivial: the Nov 11 spread is -20.6 vs -20.7 (rounding of 30.8-51.4), the historical spread average is +6 vs +6.5 (AAII's stated +6.5), and the exact release date of the final 2026 survey (Dec 30/31, possibly shifted for the holiday) is unresolved but does not matter. The remaining questions were judgment: how fast the spread reverts and how fat the right tail is. I agree with the runs' reference class and dispersion and carry them forward, setting the 90th percentile at +6.5 to allow for year-end bullish spikes like Jul 15's +12. I put 1% on a reading below -40, which happens only in crash scenarios. I retrieved nothing myself.
